title: Quantized Model Soup Shake-Up: Weight Perturbation for Enhanced Ensemble Diversity

problem.claim: Quantization-aware training can collapse independently fine-tuned models into nearly identical quantized representations, eliminating the diversity required for model soup while linear mode connectivity remains intact.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies the need to address ensemble degeneracy under quantization-aware training while preserving linear mode connectivity.

contributions.claim: The work shows analytically and empirically that fine-tuning from a sufficiently converged QAT checkpoint, termed the QAT anchor state, preserves linear mode connectivity by keeping models within the same loss basin.
The work identifies Ensemble Degeneracy as a many-to-one quantizer mapping that produces nearly identical quantized representations from independently fine-tuned models.
QMSS selectively perturbs low-magnitude weights near quantization bin boundaries, flips their integer assignments, and briefly retrains each variant through QAT.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across four datasets, two quantizers, CNNs, and Vision Transformers reportedly show consistent improvements over standard model soup.
The reported gains reach up to +1.54% Top-1 on CIFAR-100 and +2.09% on CIFAR-100-C.
The authors report over 6.37× inference speedup on a Jetson Orin Nano at 8/8-bit.

narrative_sequence.summary: Model soup provides ensemble-level accuracy at single-model inference cost but depends on linear mode connectivity and candidate diversity.
The work studies these requirements under quantization-aware training and reports that a QAT anchor state preserves linear mode connectivity.
The work identifies Ensemble Degeneracy, in which quantization removes diversity despite preserved connectivity.
QMSS perturbs unstable weights near quantization boundaries and briefly retrains variants to create quantized-domain diversity while preserving connectivity.
Experiments across datasets, quantizers, and model families report accuracy improvements and inference speedup.

source_observation.claim: A small fraction of low-magnitude weights near quantization bin boundaries can be perturbed to produce substantial quantized-domain diversity while preserving linear mode connectivity.

interpretation.claim: Targeting quantization-unstable parameters may be a focused way to restore diversity without broadly disrupting the model.

application.claim: For quantized model ensembles, consider selectively perturbing boundary-adjacent weights followed by brief QAT retraining.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the evaluated datasets, quantizers, architectures, and bit-width setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the precise perturbation-selection rule or retraining procedure.
The abstract does not report ablations isolating the effects of perturbation and retraining.
The abstract does not provide full experimental configurations or statistical variability.
